title: Evolution of a Cystic Microprolactinoma: Case Report
content: Background/Objectives: Biochemical control and radiological response may follow different trajectories during dopamine agonist treatment of a cystic prolactinoma. We describe this discordance in a woman with longitudinal endocrine and imaging assessments and two subsequent pregnancies. Case Presentation: A 28-year-old woman presented in 2015 with menstrual irregularity, headache, and prolactin of 88.76 ng/mL (reference interval, 1.9–25 ng/mL). Twenty-one prolactin measurements and six written pituitary magnetic resonance imaging reports were reviewed alongside medication and reproductive histories. A right-sided pituitary lesion contained solid and cystic components. Despite persistent prolactin elevation during several cabergoline and bromocriptine regimens, the reported solid component decreased from approximately 7 × 6 mm in 2017 to 3 × 2 mm in 2021, with a residual 3 × 3 mm cystic component. Post-polyethylene glycol results remained above the interval recorded by the laboratory. Following treatment interruption associated with a pregnancy in 2019, prolactin remained elevated in 2021 without reported lesion regrowth. It subsequently normalized to 22.8 ng/mL during cabergoline treatment. A second pregnancy occurred in 2023. Conclusions: This probable cystic microprolactinoma illustrates the need to assess hormonal, structural, and reproductive outcomes separately. Persistent modest hyperprolactinemia in a shrinking lesion does not, by itself, establish dopamine agonist resistance. Interpretation requires attention to drug exposure and the distinction between persistent disease and recurrence after documented remission.
